sections.h2: Who sends my Independence, MO property tax bill?
sections.html:
Jackson County, not the City of Independence, issues the bill. The Collection Department collects it, and the Assessment Department values the property. Independence residents pay in person at the Historic Truman Courthouse, 112 W Lexington Ave, Suite 114, Independence, MO 64050, or at the Kansas City courthouse. Both sites are open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays except county holidays.

The Collection Department's number is (816) 881-3232 and its email is Collections@jacksongov.org. For a change of name or mailing address on a real property account, call the Assessment Department at 816-881-3530. Telling the post office or the DMV about a move does not update the county tax account.

sections.h2: When is the Independence tax bill due this year?
sections.html:
Payment for tax year 2026 is due December 31, 2026, just over six weeks away. Last year the county printed bills in early November and mailed them through December 12. Jackson County says to call if yours has not arrived by December 8, and it adds that a missing bill does not excuse the debt. For a mailed payment the postmark must be December 31 or earlier, and the county advises mailing several days ahead because post office drop boxes do not always stamp the same day.

The county's 2025 notes list in-person Saturday hours in the weeks before the deadline, so check the Collection page for this year's schedule. The drop box at the south door of the Truman Courthouse locks at midnight on December 31, and cash must never go in it.

Cost to pay Jackson County property tax online (Jackson County Collection FAQ, 2025)
ItemCharge
Every online transaction$2.00
E-check (ACH), added$1.25
Debit or credit card, added2.75%
Check or money orderPayable to Jackson County Collector, with the account number

The county says it does not receive these processing fees. Online payment closes at 11:40 p.m. on December 31.

sections.h2: What happens to Independence property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Jackson County's FAQ states that taxes are a lien on the real estate and stay with the property, so a buyer becomes liable for any unpaid real estate tax. The county says taxes are generally prorated between buyer and seller at closing, and that the closing company may pay any tax currently due if it is known. Typically nothing is paid to the Collector at the moment of sale.

  • Buyers should confirm that any cash credited to them at closing is meant for the next tax bill.
  • A bill can be mailed in the seller's name unless the buyer tells the Assessor about the new owner and mailing address.
  • If a mortgage company pays through escrow, forward the bill to it.

Before listing, look up the parcel at payments.jacksongov.org and ask the Collection Department about any prior-year balance. A past-due amount appears on the current bill but is no longer itemized by year, so keep last year's bill for the detail.

sections.h2: Can I still appeal my Independence assessment for 2026?
sections.html:
The Board of Equalization appeal window for 2026 ran from May 1 to July 13, 2026 and has closed. The Board now sits at 1300 Washington in Kansas City. If you filed, you can still follow your case, and the county offers a written withdrawal form at any time.

An appeal that finishes before year end will not change this year's bill in time. The county says recalculations for 2026 appeal decisions and stipulations are suspended until January 2027, so the 2026 bill must be paid in full by December 31, 2026. A refund of any excess is then issued automatically, and you do not need to pay under protest to get it. Partial payments are accepted for real estate but cannot be made online, and interest, penalties and fees still run on any unpaid amount.

After the Board, an owner can go to the State Tax Commission, which has its own online application. Someone who signed a stipulation with the Assessor has ended the Board case and cannot go on to the Commission.

sections.h2: What is Independence, Missouri, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Independence sits on the south bank of the Missouri River, about 78 square miles in total, mostly in Jackson County with a small part reaching into Clay County. It was founded on March 29, 1827 and later became a starting point for the Santa Fe, California and Oregon trails. Harry S. Truman grew up here, and the Truman Library and the Truman home site are in the city. The 2020 census counted 123,011 people, which made Independence the fifth most populous city in Missouri.

  • Population estimate, July 1, 2025: 121,675
  • Households, 2020 to 2024: 51,477, at 2.34 people each
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 60.9%
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $172,900
  • Median gross rent: $1,109
  • Median household income: $60,339
  • Mean commute to work: 23.9 minutes

These come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for the city.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads shape a house sale in Independence?
sections.html:
Four school districts reach into the city: Independence, Blue Springs, Fort Osage and Raytown. Buyers often ask which one serves a street, and the county parcel record lists the district. Three public high schools sit inside the city limits, and Blue River Community College, part of Metropolitan Community College, has a campus here.

Interstates 70, 470 and 435 touch the area, with 435 running just outside the western edge. US 24 and US 40 form northern and southern edges, and Missouri routes 7, 12, 78 and 291 connect neighborhoods to Kansas City, Blue Springs and Lee's Summit. The city owns its electric utility, Independence Power and Light, which dates to 1901. A 2016 city financial report listed the Independence School District (2,200 employees), Northrop Grumman Innovation Systems (1,722) and Centerpoint Medical Center (1,400) as the largest employers.

sections.h2: How has the county reassessment affected Independence owners?
sections.html:
In September 2023 the Independence City Council voted to sue Jackson County over what it called inconsistent and unfair assessment processes, and it hired outside counsel to file the case. Jackson County's own FAQ now says appeal recalculations are suspended until January 2027, and Missouri statute requires the assessor to prove a value in a charter county such as Jackson if a computer or computer-assisted method set it.

Under RSMo 137.115 that proof must include an appraisal-based finding and the prices of at least three comparable sales within a mile. Owners who want to challenge a value should gather their own comparable sales and their appraisal before next year's window. The 2026 deadline fell on the second Monday in July. The Board accepts certified appraisals, sales contracts and settlement statements for recent sales, repair estimates and, for income property, rent rolls and leases, but it does not accept an opinion from a real estate agent.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax for Independence, MO?
faqs.a: The Jackson County Collection Department does. Its Independence office is in the Historic Truman Courthouse at 112 W Lexington Ave, Suite 114, and the phone is (816) 881-3232.

faqs.q: When is Independence property tax due?
faqs.a: December 31 of each year. For tax year 2026 that is December 31, 2026. Mailed payments need a USPS postmark of that date or earlier, and online payment ends at 11:40 p.m. that night.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or seller pay Independence property tax at closing?
faqs.a: The county says taxes are generally prorated between buyer and seller, and that the closing company may pay tax currently due if it is known. The new owner is liable for any unpaid real estate tax because it follows the property.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Independence property value after July?
faqs.a: The 2026 Board of Equalization window ended July 13, 2026. Pay the 2026 bill in full by December 31, and the county will refund any excess automatically if a later appeal or stipulation lowers the value.

faqs.q: How much extra does it cost to pay Independence property tax online?
faqs.a: Jackson County charges a $2.00 fee per online transaction, plus $1.25 for an e-check or 2.75 percent for a card, per its 2025 FAQ. Checks and money orders carry no such fee and go to the Jackson County Collector.
